editorial:
Five years after everything was awesome, the Lego world has turned into a dusty, Mad Max-style wasteland thanks to constant attacks from cute but destructive DUPLO invaders. Emmet is still his cheerful self, while Lucy and the others have gone tough and gritty. When a mysterious new villain named Queen Watevra Wa'Nabi shows up and kidnaps Lucy and the gang, Emmet teams up with a rugged space hero named Rex Dangervest to save them. The vibe is bright, silly, and packed with jokes that kids and adults can both enjoy.

The animation looks fantastic, with tons of clever visual gags and catchy songs that will stick in your head. The voice cast, including Chris Pratt and Elizabeth Banks, brings great energy. On the downside, the story feels a bit more scattered than the first movie, and some jokes land harder than others. Still, it's a fun ride for families and fans of the original.
endingExplained: In the final act, you learn that Rex Dangervest is actually a future version of Emmet who became bitter and hardened after being left under the washing machine. The whole conflict was really about a brother and sister fighting over toys in the real world. Once the kids learn to share and play together, the Lego world is restored. Emmet rejects his dark future self, and everything becomes awesome again as the siblings rebuild together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animated family comedies with heart and humor.
